stem: In right triangle \(ABC\) shown, angle \(C\) is a right angle, the measure of angle \(A\) is \(52^{\circ}\), and \(AC = 11\). Which expression gives the length of \(\overline{AB}\)?
solution: \(\overline{AC}\) is adjacent to angle \(A\) and \(\overline{AB}\) is the hypotenuse, so \(\cos 52^{\circ} = \frac{11}{AB}\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. \(11\cos 52^{\circ}\) would be the adjacent leg if 11 were the hypotenuse, but 11 is the adjacent leg.
explanation.B: Incorrect. \(11\tan 52^{\circ}\) is the length of the other leg, \(\overline{BC}\), not the hypotenuse.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This uses sine, but \(\overline{AC}\) is adjacent to angle \(A\), not opposite it.

verify:
P=figure['points']
d=lambda a,b: sqrt((P[a][0]-P[b][0])**2+(P[a][1]-P[b][1])**2)
ang=lambda a,v,b: N(acos(((P[a][0]-P[v][0])*(P[b][0]-P[v][0])+(P[a][1]-P[v][1])*(P[b][1]-P[v][1]))/(d(a,v)*d(b,v)))*180/pi)
assert d('A','C')==11 and abs(ang('B','A','C')-52)<0.1 and abs(ang('A','C','B')-90)<0.1
ans=11/cos(52*pi/180)
assert abs(d('A','B')-ans)<0.02
# choices use degrees: value() gives cos(52) in radians, so convert the trig arguments
deg=lambda k: N(value(choices[k]).replace(lambda e: e.func in (sin,cos,tan), lambda e: e.func(e.args[0]*pi/180)))
assert abs(deg(answer)-ans)<1e-9
assert all(abs(deg(k)-ans)>0.1 for k in choices if k!=answer)
assert abs(deg('B')-d('B','C'))<0.02 and abs(deg('A')-11*cos(52*pi/180))<1e-9
